prompt_text: I need help choosing a health insurance plan in Kansas City. Which specific brokers should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give the most useful, specific broker names and phone numbers I need two quick details:
1) Which side of Kansas City are you in (Kansas City, MO or Kansas City, KS) and your ZIP code?  
2) What kind of coverage are you shopping for: individual/family on the ACA marketplace, Medicaid/KanCare, Medicare (Part A/B + Advantage/Part D), small‑group/employer, or short‑term/limited benefit?

While you reply, here is a clear plan and immediate options so you can start calling right away.

Which types of helpers to call (and why)
- Certified Marketplace Agents / Navigators — free help enrolling in ACA plans, eligibility checks for premium tax credits, and KanCare/Medicaid screening. They’re non‑commissioned or funded to assist and can be less sales‑driven.
- Independent insurance brokers/agents — represent multiple carriers. Good if you want side‑by‑side quotes, help with network and drug formulary comparisons, and ongoing account service.
- Captive agents (carrier agents) — represent a single insurer (Blue KC, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, etc.). Useful if you already favor a carrier and want to learn their full product lineup, discounts, and provider network.
- Medicare brokers/specialists — if you’re 65+ or eligible for Medicare, use a broker who specializes in Medicare plans (they know enrollment windows, Part D formularies, and supplemental options).

Where to find reputable local brokers and helpers (quick, reliable sources)
- Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help” (or your state’s marketplace site): lists certified agents/navigators in your ZIP code. Free and neutral for ACA plans.
- Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance agent directories: search by ZIP to find licensed agents and check complaint history.
- Medicare.gov “Find a Broker/Agent” or “Medicare Plan Finder” if you need Medicare advice.
- United Way 2‑1‑1 or local community health centers often host navigator events each open enrollment season.

What to ask when you call (so you can compare quickly)
- Are you a certified Marketplace agent/navigator or a licensed broker? (Navigator = free help; broker = may earn a commission.)
- Which carriers do you represent? (Independent = multiple carriers; captive = one.)
- Do you have experience with my specific needs? (Medicare, marketplace subsidies, specific doctors/hospitals)
- Will you run total monthly premium + deductible + out‑of‑pocket max comparisons and check prescription formularies?
- Do you provide ongoing service after enrollment (claims help, renewals, mid‑year changes)?
- What are your fees or how are you paid?

Documents to have ready when you call
- ZIP code and preferred doctors/hospitals
- List of regular medications (name, dose)
- Estimated household income (for marketplace subsidies)
- Date of birth (for Medicare eligibility)

If you tell me your ZIP and which kind of coverage, I’ll look up a short vetted list of specific local brokers/agency names and the best number(s) to call, plus one or two carrier agents to compare. Which ZIP and plan type should I search for?
